name: start_operation
description: Run one human-confirmed domain preview in a background operation. Set toolName to the previewed tool; arguments contains only dryRun=false and its planId. Omit both sessionId/changeSetId for server-managed ownership, or supply an owned open pair. Retain operationId. If the start response is lost, repeat the identical start with the same planId: the already started operation is returned with alreadyStarted=true and nothing is written again. This is not an exactly-once guarantee; after node failure the write outcome may be UNKNOWN. A refused start returns errorCode PREVIEW_STALE with staleReason: EXPIRED (your preview is older than its time limit) or NOT_FOUND (no such preview for you and this tool): obtain a new preview and a fresh confirmation. CONSUMED means this planId was already applied with a different toolName: check toolName, never retry the write; preview again if the change is still needed. A domain tool may also return PREVIEW_STALE when Jira changed after the preview: preview again. A terminal response with domain result needs no get_operation; otherwise poll get_operation until terminal. Disconnect does not stop work. Never locate an operation or object by name-search or repeating create. The bounded executor may reject a full queue before starting work. After a successful operation answer in 1–3 sentences: what was done and whether the result differs from the confirmed plan. Never repeat tables of fields, screens, assignments or limitations the user already confirmed; a create report table (ids and links) is the only table, as it is new. Then show only the next preview. Errors, partial results and new warnings are reported in full.

name: get_operation
description: Read persisted status and domain result of an owned operation by its operationId, including after reconnecting. Without an operationId (lost start response) repeat the identical start_operation with the same planId; it returns the started operation. QUEUED/RUNNING/CANCEL_REQUESTED are not completion. The server waits up to waitSeconds (default 20) and returns as soon as the operation is terminal. If it is still QUEUED/RUNNING/CANCEL_REQUESTED, call get_operation again right away. Never wait by other means (sleep, timers, scripts, web requests). Stop checking on a terminal state. Report the domain result; do not claim that a failed or partial operation changed nothing. Node failure may leave the write outcome UNKNOWN; there is no exactly-once guarantee. Preserve reported warnings, errors and partial changes.

waitSeconds.description: Maximum server wait in seconds; defaults to 20. Use 0 for an immediate status read.
